analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/startup-shape-warmup.md, lines 1-3) and a doc addition in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 557-564). No executable source was supplied, so the actual warmup implementation, the proactive MLX pool sweep deferral, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env parsing could not be reviewed.

The documented behavior is a startup shape warmup. It runs after model load and self-test, before the provider registers or the local listener opens. It reuses the existing calibration session, idle gate and foreground lease, and stays within the same KV and service budgets. It publishes no observations or work totals. The doc says a customer request cancels it and waits for retirement, which matches the existing foreground-admission contract. It uses synthetic inputs, so it should not touch consumer prompts (A-001). It writes no prefix cache entries as described, so T-041 is unaffected. It does not change attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053, T-054), or coordinator wire fields. It adds no new env knob beyond a disable/always toggle. Nothing here weakens registration gating, because the warmup precedes registration. The availability implication is bounded: 20 seconds maximum, and the listener and registration are delayed only until warmup completes.

Open items for integration or the next pass:
(1) Confirm the warmup uses synthetic tokens and does not donate to the SSD prefix cache (T-041). Otherwise it could write at-rest artifacts or create a TTFT oracle.
(2) Confirm warmup memory is admitted through the process ledger and does not bypass the activation reserve.
(3) Confirm that deferring the proactive MLX pool sweep during any session cannot starve memory reclamation under pressure. The doc says on-pressure reclaims still run.
(4) Confirm that the startup delay (up to 20 seconds per model) does not interact badly with App Attest or challenge timeouts.
No concrete regression is visible from the docs alone.
